Keep the current change in view.

CodeRabbit Change Stack · Formbricks #8650 · Parth Pawar

A reviewer must locate the change, inspect its evidence, and decide what to do next. I kept Change Stack’s layer model and reorganized the screen around that sequence. Four observations from the assigned PR drove the design.

ObservationDecision and reason
Layer and file navigation require repeated orientation.Keep the selected layer, file, and path together. Disclose the nine-file list on demand so the rail stays scannable.
Several toolbars compete with the diff.Group frequent file actions in one sticky toolbar. Keep Submit review in the PR header; secondary capabilities retain labeled destinations.
Summary scope is easy to misread: 37 in the layer, six for access.ts.Label file and layer scope. Preserve existing summary-to-code linking and use matching selection to show the active range.
Summary seen, file viewed, and final review are distinct progress signals.Give each a separate action and count. Opening a file does not mark it viewed. A review decision requires an explicit dialog.

Tradeoff

Persistent context costs code width. Z hides the side panels while preserving position; below 1280 px, context becomes an overlay. Keeping layers preserves a familiar review order and avoids adding a new review workflow.

Validation

The prototype checks linked selection, reversible progress, keyboard navigation, and focus restoration. Next, test whether developers can locate a file, connect a summary to code, and explain what remains to review. No measured usability gain is claimed.

Formbricks #8650, pinned snapshot 23cdac2 (out of date). Seven of 52 file diffs are included; other content is labeled as preview. Complete capability parity is unverified. Reviews are simulated and nothing is sent.
